### `Rendered`  <sub>data</sub>

```
Rendered := Midi Int Int Int
    Perc Int Int
```

A committed, playable event: program, key, velocity.  Concrete because
MIDI is the only backend; this type is the seam where another would go.
`Midi` is a pitched note on some program; `Perc` is an unpitched one.
The distinction is musical, not a transport detail — percussion is a
different *kind* of sound, and which MIDI channel carries it is the
renderer's business (`gestate/midi.py`).


### `Score`  <sub>data</sub>

```
Score a := Note a                # `'x` — unassigned, carries the payload
    Play Rendered         # committed to MIDI: parametric in `a`
    Assigned Voice        # committed to a `voices` bank; likewise
    Rest
    Seq (Score a) (Score a)
    Par (Score a) (Score a)   # `||` — at the same time
    At Int (Score a)
    Scale (Score a) Int
    Shrink (Score a) Int
    Retro (Score a)          # `reverse` — back to front
    Sown (Int -> Score a)     # `sown f` — one beat, seed decides
    Sow Int (Score a)         # `sow n s` — re-root a subtree's seed
    Clip Int (Score a)        # content clipped to a declared span
    Mark Int                  # `mark n` — a bar point, zero wide
    Probe Int (List Int -> Score a)
```


### `ticksPerBeat`

```
ticksPerBeat : Int
```

**Ticks to the beat.**  96 divides by 2,3,4,6,8,12,16,24,32,48, so every
division anyone writes is exact — and the whole score is laid out in
these, so a bar of four is `4 * ticksPerBeat`.

It was `beat`, and the plain word has gone to the *audio* side, where
`beat : Sig Float` is what time it is in beats.  Two things called
"beat" is one too many, and of the two this is the one that is really a
resolution rather than a beat.

### `Semigroup (Score b)`  <sub>instance</sub>

```
instance Semigroup (Score b) where
```

`++` is *music sequence* here, shadowing the core prelude's list append.
A class with two instances would be the general answer and is not needed:
An *instance* rather than a redefinition, which is what stops it hiding
the prelude's list append — see `prelude.ges`, where `++` is now
`Semigroup`'s method.  A music program has both again.

### `Reversible Score`  <sub>instance</sub>

```
instance Reversible Score where
```

**Retrograde** — the phrase backwards, which is the third of the four
things a canon does to a subject.

A *constructor* rather than a walk that turns the tree inside out, and
`||` is why: an overlay is **left-aligned**, so reversing `a || b`
structurally would leave two voices of unequal length still starting
together, when what a retrograde means is that they still *end*
together.  The duration is not known until the subtree is laid out, so
the mirror happens where the duration is — in `layOnto`, against the
events, exactly as `Scale` does.

`reverse` and not `retrograde`, because that is what this operation is
called everywhere else it appears; `prelude.ges` has the class and the
list instance.


### `at`

```
at : Int -> [: a :] -> [: a :]
```

`at` translates a score's *extent* and leaves its *duration* alone, which
is why `a ++ at (-1) b` overlaps `a` without moving what follows.

### `Monad Score`  <sub>instance</sub>

```
instance Monad Score where
```

Substitute a score for each *unassigned* note.  `Play` is left alone —
it carries no payload — which is why "ignored if an instrument is already
selected" needs no runtime mark.
An *instance*, for the reason `++` above is one.  A score's `pure` is
`Note`, which is exactly what `'x` already writes.


### `prog`

```
prog : Int -> Int -> [: b :]
```

**A MIDI program number, as an instrument.**  `melody >>= prog 73`
commits every unassigned note in `melody` to program 73 — a flute.

An instrument is any function from a note's payload to a committed
score, applied with `>>=`; this is the one that names a MIDI program,
and `percussion` is the other.  A score bound with one holds no payload,
so it is parametric and unifies with `Void` — which is what makes it
performable.

Named `prog` and not `instrument` because a composer wants that word:
this file is prepended as *text*, so a piece that defines its own
`instrument` would have collided with the library rather than shadowed
it, and "instrument" is the first thing anyone reaches for when naming
the four voices of a quartet.


### `percussion`

```
percussion : Int -> [: b :]
```

The percussion instrument.  It needs no program number, so it is itself
the function `>>=` wants: `pattern >>= percussion`.

## Tempo


### `Tempo`  <sub>type alias</sub>

```
type Tempo = Envelope
```

**A tempo *is* an envelope** — of beats per minute, against beats — so
this is `audio.ges`'s `Envelope` under the name a piece calls it by,
rather than a second type with the same two constructors.  Declaring it
twice would give a scored program two `Step`s, and a constructor's name
is the whole program's.


## Forever is a value — `spec/dynamicscore.md`, stage two


### `cycle`

```
cycle : [: a :] -> [: a :]
```

`cycle bar` is `bar`, then `cycle bar` — which the lazy machine only
ever builds as far as somebody plays it.  Nothing here is new to the
language; what is new is a performer that stops demanding.


### `unfold`

```
unfold : b -> (b -> ([: a :], b)) -> [: a :]
```

A generative score: `unfold seed next`, where `next` grows one section
and the state the following one grows from.  Seed it and it is
replayable — the transcript records the seed, not the surprise.


### `streamVoices`

```
streamVoices : [: Void :] -> List (Int, Int, Voice)
```

The stream a dynamic performance forces — `layVoices`' twin, an event
list in **beat order, lazy in its tail**, so a performer can force
enough to cover the next few beats and no more.  Like `layVoices` it
is named by a generated entry point (`streamMain`), which is why it
stays above the marker; the walk it fronts is below.


### `liveVoices`

```
liveVoices : [: Void :] -> List Cue
```

The stream a *listening* performance forces — `streamVoices` with one
more power: it can end in a question.  A `CueAsk` is a probe reached:
its continuation holds **the entire rest of the performance**, so the
host answers it with the port's reading at the downbeat and simply
keeps walking the list the answer returns.  No rebuilding, no second
walk — the question is the spine, suspended.


## Reading the seed — `spec/dynamicscore.md`, stage three


### `sown`

```
sown : (Int -> [: a :]) -> [: a :]
```

**A leaf whose content the seed decides.**  One beat, like every
leaf; `|*` and `|/` scale it; content longer than the span is
clipped.  What varies is what sounds — never how long it takes,
which is what keeps a chancy score seekable and bakeable.


### `sow`

```
sow : Int -> [: a :] -> [: a :]
```

Re-root a subtree's seed: `sow 7 intro ++ improvisation` is fixed
art inside an improvisation.


### `long`

```
long : Int -> [: a :] -> [: a :]
```

**A declared span: this branch is `n` beats long, whatever its
content does.**  `long 16 verse` pins the verse to sixteen beats —
content past the box is clipped, content short of it rests out the
difference — which is the stage-three invariant handed to the
author: content bends, time doesn't.

The declaration pays twice.  Today it is structure a reader can
trust; next it is what lets a performer *skip*: a branch whose width
is written down can be passed over without forcing what is inside,
so resuming a long-running piece descends by arithmetic instead of
unfolding from the left.  (`sown` sections carry this box already —
every decision is born clipped.)


### `mark`

```
mark : Int -> [: a :]
```

**A bar point** — zero beats wide, so `mark 1 ++ verse` moves
nothing.  A mark is a place the music can be re-entered: the
performer enumerates them (`streamMarks`, below with the walks)
without touching a single note, and a resume names one instead of
unfolding everything to its left.  Numbered rather than named,
the way seeds are: what matters is that the same one means the
same place twice.


### `bar`

```
bar : [: a :]
```

**An anonymous bar point** — `bar ++ verse ++ bar ++ chorus` marks
the seams without naming them.  Anonymity works because a resume
goes to the nearest point by *tick*, never by number; the
enumeration numbers these left to right for a human to point at,
which shifts when marks are added — a place that must keep its
name across edits writes `mark n` instead.


### `Port`  <sub>type alias</sub>

```
type Port = Int
```

**Which reading a `probe` asks for.**  An alias of `Int` for the
reason `Seed` is over in `synth.ges`: the number is an identity the
expander assigns (`holds.<bank>` is port `k` for the `k`-th bank),
and what the name buys is a signature that says which integer is
wanted.


### `probe`

```
probe : Port -> (List Int -> [: a :]) -> [: a :]
```

**A leaf whose content the world decides** — `probe holds.lead f`
plays `f` of whatever keys the lead port holds *at this leaf's own
downbeat*.  One beat, like every leaf; `|*` and `|/` scale it;
content past the box is clipped: the stage-three invariant again —
what varies is what sounds, never how long it takes.  A probe can
not be forced early — the reading does not exist yet — so the
performance decides exactly as late as the author wrote (`|/ 4`
listens every sixteenth), and every reading lands in the transcript,
which is what makes an improvisation replayable.


### `streamMarks`

```
streamMarks : [: Void :] -> List (Int, Int)
```

Every mark and where it falls, `(tick, mark)`, beat-ordered and
lazy — `streamVoices`' little sibling, named by its own generated
entry (`marksMain`), which is why it stands above the marker.


### `resumeAt`

```
resumeAt : Int -> [: a :] -> [: a :]
```

**The remainder of a score from tick `t` on** — what a resume plays,
with `t` rebased to zero.  The walk *descends by declared widths*:
a `Clip` whose box ends before `t` is skipped without forcing one
thing inside it, which is what turns resuming a long-running piece
from an unfolding into an arithmetic.  Run on the **sown** tree
(`resumeMain` composes it after `sowScore`), so every surviving
subtree keeps exactly the seed its position always had.

Two honest slops, both bounded by where resumes happen (beat and
bar points): a cut inside `Scale k` floors to the nearest multiple
of `k`, and a cut *into* a retrograde keeps it whole — a mirror has
no remainder that is not also a different piece.


### `resumeSeq`


One value, drawn whole from a seed — the class is what lets an
author's payload be drawn the way it is built, one split per field.
An instance receives a seed it owns outright; what it does not
`split` it must not reuse.

### `sowScore`

```
sowScore : Int -> [: a :] -> [: a :]
```

**Where the seed enters the tree** — named by the generated entry
points beside `layVoices` and `streamVoices`, which is why it stays
above the marker.  A score with no `sown` in it passes through
unchanged whatever the seed, which is what keeps fixed art fixed.

### Reading the seed — `spec/dynamicscore.md`, stage three


#### `maxInt`

#### `placeScaled`

```
placeScaled : Int -> Int -> List (Int, Int, Rendered) -> List (Int, Int, Rendered)
```

Scaling a subtree's events into place: `placeScaled off k es` puts local
coordinate `x` of a scaled subtree at `off + x*k`.  Only `Scale` and `Shrink` need this —
translation composes with the offset `layOnto` already carries, so there
is no `shiftEvents` any more.

These destructure in the lambda rather than projecting: a lambda
parameter's type is not known at a projection site — `map`'s
instantiation settles it later, and projection is resolved from the type
(`fixme.md` F28) — while a pattern needs no such knowledge, which is what
the error message says to do.

```

```

the same idea `placeScaled` is `Scale`'s.

### The unfolding half — `spec/dynamicscore.md`, stage two


#### `durOf`

```
durOf : [: a :] -> Int
```

A score's **duration in ticks, from its shape alone** — no events are
laid to answer it, which is what lets a sequence stream: the right
half's offset needs the left half's duration, not its notes.
The algebra is `layVoicesOnto`'s, separated from the laying: `at`
translates extent and leaves duration alone, an overlay lasts as long
as its longer branch, and every leaf — even a rest — is one beat.


#### `mergeVoices`

```
mergeVoices : List (Int, Int, Voice) -> List (Int, Int, Voice) -> List (Int, Int, Voice)
```

Two beat-ordered streams as one.  **Left-biased** on a shared onset,
which keeps an overlay's branches in writing order at the instant they
coincide — the same order the eager layout gives a stable sort, so the
allocator makes the same choices either way.


#### `streamVoicesAt`

```
streamVoicesAt : Int -> [: a :] -> List (Int, Int, Voice)
```

The primitive, because the fold below cost 64 case-splits per call
and a resume descends through two mix64s *per spine level* — 71
seconds of rejoin were measured before this line.  `xorGo` stays as
the primitive's written-out meaning: what `prim_xor_int` computes,
what `crust`'s `XorInt` is held to, and what either would be checked
against if they ever disagreed.
